identity.title: Interactive Cross-modal Learning for Text-3D Scene Retrieval

problem.claim: Retrieve relevant 3D scenes from linguistic queries despite incomplete user descriptions.

gap.claim: Existing T3SR methods implicitly assume information-complete queries, which is difficult to obtain in practical deployments and can degrade performance.

contributions.claim: Proposes IDeal, an interactive text–3D scene retrieval method that iteratively improves text–scene alignment.
Introduces IRR, using successive questioner–answerer rounds for detailed probing or exploratory divergence, followed by feature- and semantic-level fusion for scene reranking.
Introduces IAT for contrastive domain adaptation between queries and interactive texts, addressing discriminability and diversity risks in augmented text features.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe IDeal as a novel interactive retrieval method centered on continuous interaction for text–3D scene alignment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on three datasets demonstrating IDeal's superiority.

narrative_sequence.summary: T3SR retrieves relevant scenes from linguistic queries.
Traditional methods assume complete query descriptions, whereas practical users and models may not provide them.
IDeal addresses this through continuous interaction, with IRR conducting successive questioner–answerer refinement rounds and multimodal fusion.
IAT adapts augmented interactive-text features toward the interaction-text domain using contrastive learning.
The authors report results across three datasets and provide code.

source_observation.claim: The paper separates interactive query refinement from domain adaptation: IRR generates and fuses interaction information, while IAT addresses the resulting query-domain mismatch.

lessons.interpretation: This decomposition can make a multimodal retrieval proposal easier to explain and align each component with a distinct failure mode.
lessons.application: When proposing an interactive retrieval system, explicitly map each module to either information acquisition, representation fusion, or domain alignment, then evaluate those roles separately.
lessons.exception: This decomposition may be unsuitable when interaction text is already in-domain or when the application cannot support multi-round questioning.

unknowns: No dataset names, metrics, baselines, numerical results, or ablation findings are given, so the reported superiority cannot be quantified or attributed to individual components.
The abstract does not specify how questions and answers are generated or how many interaction rounds are used.
